events.title: Ponce de León Sights Florida
events.description: Spanish explorer Juan Ponce de León spotted and then landed on the Florida coast near present-day St. Augustine, naming the land La Florida during the Easter season (Pascua Florida).
events.significance: Marked the first well-documented European arrival in what is now the continental United States and began Spanish colonization efforts in North America.

events.title: U.S. Coinage Act Establishes the Mint
events.description: President George Washington signed the Coinage Act, creating the United States Mint in Philadelphia and establishing the U.S. dollar as the national currency on a decimal system.
events.significance: Established the foundations of the American monetary system and national control over coinage.

events.title: Birth of Hans Christian Andersen
events.description: Danish author Hans Christian Andersen was born in Odense, Denmark. He went on to write fairy tales such as The Little Mermaid, The Ugly Duckling, and The Emperor's New Clothes.
events.significance: His tales became some of the most widely translated and enduring works of world literature, influencing children's literature and popular culture worldwide.

events.title: Argentina Invades the Falkland Islands
events.description: Argentine forces landed on the Falkland Islands, a British overseas territory in the South Atlantic, beginning the Falklands War between Argentina and the United Kingdom.
events.significance: The 74-day conflict ended in British victory, contributed to the fall of Argentina's military junta, and strengthened Margaret Thatcher's government in the UK.

events.title: Death of Pope John Paul II
events.description: Pope John Paul II died in Vatican City at age 84 after a long illness, ending a pontificate of nearly 27 years that began in 1978.
events.significance: As the first non-Italian pope in centuries and a major global figure, he influenced the end of Cold War communism in Europe and interfaith relations; his funeral drew one of the largest gatherings in history.
